title: Total Appeal of A String
statement: Define the **appeal** of a string as how many different characters it contains (so `"abbca"` has appeal 3, from `a`, `b` and `c`). Given a string `s`, consider every substring of `s` (every contiguous, non-empty run of characters, counting equal substrings at different positions separately) and return the sum of their appeals.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Listing every substring and counting its distinct letters is O(n²) at best. Flip the view: instead of asking "how many letters does each substring have", ask "how many substrings does each letter count in". A distinct letter is counted once per substring, so charge it to its **first** occurrence inside that substring. Position `i` is the first copy of `s[i]` in a substring exactly when the substring starts after the previous copy of that letter and at or before `i`, and ends anywhere from `i` onward.

## Approach

1. Keep `last[letter]`, the most recent index of each letter, starting at `-1`.
2. For each `i`, `startChoices = i - last[letter]` counts the start positions after the previous copy, up to `i`.
3. `endChoices = n - i` counts the end positions from `i` to the end.
4. Their product is the number of substrings in which `s[i]` is the first copy of its letter; add it to `total`.
5. Record `i` as the latest index of this letter.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "abbca"`, `n = 5`.

| i | char | last before | startChoices | endChoices | added |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | a | -1 | 1 | 5 | 5 |
| 1 | b | -1 | 2 | 4 | 8 |
| 2 | b | 1 | 1 | 3 | 3 |
| 3 | c | -1 | 4 | 2 | 8 |
| 4 | a | 0 | 4 | 1 | 4 |

`5 + 8 + 3 + 8 + 4 = 28`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant work per character.
- Space: O(1): a fixed table of 26 indices.

## Pitfalls

- Starting `last` at `0` instead of `-1` undercounts the start positions for a letter's first appearance by one.
- Charging every occurrence (not just the first) counts repeated letters several times in one substring.
- The total grows to about 10^11, past 32-bit range; use `long` in Java and `long long` in C.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `s` |
| `last` | latest index of each letter seen so far, or `-1` |
| `letter` | 0–25 code of `s[i]` |
| `startChoices` | starts that keep `s[i]` as the first copy |
| `endChoices` | ends that include `s[i]` |
| `total` | running sum of appeals |

narration.3: No letter has been seen yet, so every last index starts at -1.
narration.7: Turn the character into an index from 0 to 25.
narration.8: Substrings may start anywhere after the previous copy of this letter, up to i.
narration.9: They may end anywhere from i to the last character.
narration.10: Each such substring counts this letter once through position i.
narration.11: Remember i as the latest copy of this letter for later positions.
narration.13: Every substring's distinct letters have been charged exactly once.
